outcome: severe maternal complications (HELLP syndrome, eclampsia, renal failure, pulmonary edema, DIC, placental abruption)
neonatal outcomes (preterm labor, RDS, neonatal death, IUGR leading to early delivery before 34 weeks)
cohort: The study included 146 pregnant women with suspected preeclampsia (PE) at 20-33 weeks of gestation.
finding: An sFlt-1/PlGF ratio >= 85 combined with circulating ANXA2 < 6.13 ng/mL accurately identifies women at high risk for PE-related adverse outcomes, demonstrating superior early warning efficacy compared to single-biomarker strategies.
followup_time: Observations were taken up to the closest adverse outcome event or the last measurement before delivery; neonatal outcomes imply observations after birth, but a specific duration is not mentioned.
gest_age: Maternal gestational age at recruitment was 20-33 weeks; an outcome was early delivery before 34 weeks of gestation.
